_comment: PERF.1 step 6: ceilings checked by budget.ts in CI over a synthetic home at --scale 0.1. Generous on purpose (shared CI runners); a regression of the kind PERF.1 removed (a 3 s poll, a whole-file read per open, a 9 MB history response, a stale first frame) lands far above them.
_comment_storm: The rebuild storm (storm.ts): 10 sessions writing every 500 ms over a git-backed synthetic home. Before the fix, measured on the reference machine: build p50 397 ms (one git spawn pair per project per build), rebuild duty 20 %, /api/fleet p95 389 ms, echo p95 822 ms; after: 98 ms, 5 %, 61 ms, 392 ms.
_comment_startup: Fast startup (startup.ts): ms from /api/health answering to the first /api/data?partial=1 + /api/team/session — what the web app waits on before it paints — on a fresh install (cold) AND a restart (warm), over an EMPTY home and over a git home whose every `git log --numstat` takes 20 s. Before: cold first screen 2.3 s on a small synthetic home and NEVER (connection dropped at 120 s, 180 s, 240 s) with slow git; after: 0.4-0.9 s and full data in ~6 s.
_comment_engineMap: F0.4: the ENGINE.MAP bench (scripts/perf/engine-map/) — 09 §8 of the engine-map design, a mixed fleet of fake claude/codex/gemini/copilot/kimi/agy sessions on a throwaway server. Checked by engine-map/check.ts, NOT by budget.ts (which skips this object). level 'warn' reports an exceeded budget and keeps the job green; Phase 4 (F4) flips each to 'fail'. The figures are the ADAPTER-path targets of 09 §8, so a runner that is slower than the reference machine will warn — that is what a warning is for.
